architecture_note: v7 removed the 8-gate Holm-Bonferroni architecture (statistical_design.no_gate_hierarchy: true). There is no alpha/8 and no gate family to calibrate. The single frozen pass/fail rule is the composite DSR; every per-metric threshold below is reported as reference-only and is never compared against a corrected alpha.

composite_decoupling_probe.method: hold the Arm C return series and weight path fixed; sweep hmm_ari / swap_churn / tca_bps / probation_pass_rate across their full frozen ranges (320 combinations)
composite_decoupling_probe.question: does composite_score determine `passed` in CompositeGateEngine.evaluate_composite_dsr?
composite_decoupling_probe.verdict: DECOUPLED: `passed` is identical across all 320 composite-input combinations (composite_score moves over [0.0506, 0.4506] while the DSR takes 1 distinct value(s) that depend only on the return series). The composite is computed, reported, and never read by the decision.

findings: DECISION RULE CONTROLLED: null pass rate 0.000000 (Wilson upper 0.000384) is at or below the 1/N=0.001949 it claims, on a ~beta-1 zero-alpha book.

POWER / MDE: the frozen rule reaches 80% power at a true annualised Sharpe of 2.52 on the full 84-month record (90% at 3.12), on fat-tailed returns, 2000 draws per point, measured by calling the shipped DSR at N=513. Measured type-I error at a true Sharpe of 0 is 0.0.

FWER SCALE, EXPLICIT: the frozen design's own rate is 1/513 = 0.001949 (nominal_source: 1 / dsr.n_trials (N=513)). If the intended control is instead a familywise 0.05 across all 513 decisions, the per-decision alpha required is 9.75e-05 -- 513x tighter than 0.05. The two are not interchangeable; this report measures against 1/N and does not apply the other.

ZERO PER-GATE THRESHOLDS CALIBRATED, DELIBERATELY: v7 froze `no_gate_hierarchy: true` and removed the `gates:` block, so there is no per-gate family and no alpha/8 to spend. Every per-metric threshold in `reference_thresholds` is measured (threshold vs empirical null alpha is tabulated) but is labelled threshold_reference_only and is not a hypothesis test. Producing calibrated per-gate thresholds would re-introduce the architecture the frozen pre-registration deleted.

COMPOSITE SCORE DOES NOT DECIDE THE GATE (MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED): holding the Arm C return series fixed and sweeping every non-return composite input across its full frozen range (320 combinations), `passed` took 1 distinct value(s) while composite_score moved over [0.0506, 0.4506] and the DSR took 1 distinct value(s) that depend only on the return series. CompositeGateEngine sets passed = composite_dsr >= threshold on the RAW Arm C returns; the seven weighted components are computed, reported, and then never read. The frozen contract says 'statistical_design: 'DSR (Deflated Sharpe Ratio) on COMPOSITE_SCORE''; the code DSRs the returns. Either the code or the document is wrong, and the gap is load-bearing: the composite carries 0.85 of the stated design weight and 0 of the decision.

CROSS-CHECK (empirical) UNAVAILABLE: no null draw in 10000 cleared DSR>=0.95, so there is no pass set to compare composite scores across. The deterministic probe above is the load-bearing evidence and does not depend on any null passing.

THE NULL IS A MARKET-BETA BOOK: mean market beta 1.0007 (p05 1.0005, p95 1.0009) and mean annualised Sharpe 0.3301 across 10000 zero-alpha draws. Every null 'failure' below the threshold is therefore a strategy that simply did not ride beta, and every null 'pass' is one that did. This is the correct adversarial null for a Sharpe-style gate and it is why the decision rule is not trivially safe.

THRESHOLD REFERENCE (not alpha-calibrated): drawdown passes 0.2145, swap churn 0.3238, TCA 0.9878, probation band 1.0. Mean one-way turnover per rebalance is 0.4998 against the frozen execution.max_turnover_per_rebalance cap of 0.30 — a pure Dirichlet null is MAXIMALLY churning, so a high turnover failure rate here is the null working, not the gate being strict.

PROBATION BAND IS NEAR-VACUOUS: [0.35, 0.65] contains the null mean 0.50, and at the frozen evidence floor n=400 the sampling sd is only 0.0250. The band cannot separate a null run from a real one and must not be relied on alone.

HMM ARI NULL IS GENERATED, NOT ASSUMED: ARI>=0.45 on >=3/4 folds fires on 0.0000 of null draws. Under 'no regime structure' the true labels and the recovered labels are both i.i.d. uniform over 3 states, so this rate is the exact ARI-of-two-random-partitions distribution and it needs no correction — unlike the p-value gates the frozen design deleted.

CALMAR IS NOT A FROZEN v7 GATE: threshold included because the Phase-9C dispatch names it, but it was deleted with the `gates:` block in the pre-registration that v7 superseded. It is reported as a diagnostic. The same applies to the HMM occupancy caps.

fold_4_true_oos.conjunctive_note: The frozen success rule is CONJUNCTIVE (whole record AND Fold 4). Its null rate is the product of the two rates only if the two tests were independent; they are computed on overlapping data, so the measured conjunctive rate below is the number to quote, not a product of the marginals.

frozen_design.meaning: the per-decision false-positive rate the DSR inflates for, after deflating 513 trials. This is the quantity the frozen design specifies and the one measured against the null above.

if_the_intended_control_is_familywise_0..note: 0.05/513 = 9.75e-05, not 0.05. A run that treats 0.05 as the per-decision alpha after already accounting for 513 trials is 513x looser than the frozen design. Reported so the two scalings cannot be confused; NOT applied, because changing alpha is a pre-registration change.

fwer_accounting.why_zero: v7 froze `no_gate_hierarchy: true` and deleted the `gates:` block, so there are no per-gate thresholds to calibrate to a corrected alpha. Calibrating them would re-introduce the architecture the pre-registration removed. The per-metric entries in `reference_thresholds` are measured for power planning only and are explicitly not tests.

null_model.ari_null: two independent uniform 3-state partitions of 12 obs per fold (4 folds)
null_model.description: 1500 names, 84 monthly rebalances over the frozen primary window 2018-01-01..2024-12-31. Every name has exactly zero alpha; returns are beta*factor + idiosyncratic noise. Weights are i.i.d. Dirichlet(1.0) re-drawn every month (no selection, no persistence, no timing skill), so the null book is ~beta 1 to the market with maximal churn. Portfolio returns are charged 60bps per unit of one-way turnover.

power_analysis.conjunctive_note: The frozen rule is CONJUNCTIVE (whole record AND Fold 4). A conjunction's power is at most the weaker limb's, so the Fold-4 MDE quoted here is the honest floor for a claim that has to survive 2024 TRUE OOS as well as the full record. On 12 monthly observations against a 513-trial deflation, that limb needs a materially larger Sharpe than the 84-month limb does.

distributions.t5: Student-t df=5, variance-matched to the same monthly sigma 0.0430. The DSR's V term reads sample skew and RAW kurtosis, so tail shape moves the required Sharpe; the normal arm alone would flatter the gate.

mde_grid_exhausted.note: The grid tops out at 8.00; extend P9_POWER_SR_GRID before quoting this as an unbounded statement.

power_analysis.method: Monte Carlo through the shipped ingestion.harness.gate_engine.deflated_sharpe_ratio with n_trials=513 and threshold=0.95; the formula is called, not restated. Monthly volatility pinned to the frozen null DGP (0.0430); only the drift varies. The t arm is variance-matched to the normal arm so the two differ in tail SHAPE only.
power_analysis.question: what is the smallest true annualized Sharpe at which the frozen composite DSR fires? (minimum detectable effect)
power_analysis.reporting_arm_rationale: Both arms are reported. t5 is the conservative one and is what the MDE headline quotes, because a real equity book's 84 monthly returns are fat-tailed and the DSR penalises that in V.
